title: metadata-04: filter paths at any depth, reject bad ~
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 allows filter paths at any depth and requires rejecting malformed paths.

-04 §3.6 MetadataTextMatch.path: "a namespace identifier, optionally followed by a JSON Pointer [RFC6901] into the namespace value (for example, <namespace>, <namespace>/<key> or <namespace>/<key>/<subkey>). Object members are addressed by name; a path that would traverse an array or a scalar addresses no value. A path that is not well formed (for example, one with an invalid ~ escape) MUST be rejected with an "invalidArguments" error."
-04 §3.6 metadataExists: "A path, with the syntax defined for MetadataTextMatch."
(-02 limited paths to <namespace> or <namespace>/<key>.)

Affected:
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:46-56 resolve_path uses split_once('/'), so "ns/a/b" looks up a single key "a/b" instead of walking ns -> a -> b. Walk every segment; when a segment lands on an array or a scalar, return None.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:30-36 unescape_rfc6901 accepts invalid escapes (a "~" not followed by 0 or 1). -04 requires invalidArguments for those, so callers need a fallible check. Proposed: an additive pub fn (for example, a path validator returning Result/bool) so the existing bool predicates metadata_path_exists/metadata_text_contains/metadata_text_equals (filter.rs:80, 116, 145) keep their signatures.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:80-92 metadata_path_exists namespace-only branch: -04 keeps "present and not {}". Only multi-segment paths change.
- Docs that state the -02 two-segment form: crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/filter.rs:40-52 (MetadataTextMatch), :125-126 (WithMetadata.metadata_exists); crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:40-41.
- Tests: add deep-path, array-traversal (None) and invalid-~ cases. Oracle: the -04 §3.6 text above and RFC 6901 §4.

Related -04 §3.6 change, no code needed: "Conditions are evaluated against the stored data whether or not the namespace is supported". The helpers already ignore support, but the module docs should not imply otherwise.
